key_insight: A Vision Transformer–based segmentation model (USFM framework) shows robust, cross-validated performance for delineating pancreatic tumors on public endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) datasets, helping reduce operator-dependent variability in EUS interpretation.
problem_solved: Addresses variability and subjectivity in tumor delineation on EUS images that limit reliable diagnosis, quantification, and downstream clinical decision support.
method: Segmentation model implemented with the USFM framework using a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone.
Trained on 17,367 annotated EUS images aggregated from two public datasets.
Evaluated with 5-fold cross-validation using standard segmentation metrics (e.g., Dice, IoU, sensitivity/specificity) to assess robustness.
impact: Demonstrates a scalable transformer-based approach for automated, reproducible pancreatic tumor segmentation in EUS — useful for benchmarking, integrating into clinical workflows, and enabling downstream AI tasks (staging, treatment planning).
visual_elements: Model architecture schematic showing USFM pipeline with Vision Transformer backbone and segmentation head.
EUS image panels with ground-truth mask vs model prediction overlay (before/after heatmap).
Bar chart or boxplots of key segmentation metrics (Dice, IoU) across 5 folds and/or versus baseline methods.
Dataset summary infographic (total images, number per dataset, split for training/validation/testing).
paper_title: Performance of a Deep Learning-Based Segmentation Model for Pancreatic Tumors on Public Endoscopic Ultrasound Datasets
paper_authors: Pankaj Gupta, Priya Mudgil, Niharika Dutta, Kartik Bose, Nitish Kumar
